claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is obtained by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial Co-free alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
The initial Co-free alloy has equiaxed grains similar to those of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi baseline.
Dynamic deformation of Co-free FeNiCrMn produces an ultra-nanocrystalline layer at grain boundaries or other internal interfaces.
Dynamic deformation of Co-free FeNiCrMn can produce a partially amorphous layer at grain boundaries or other internal interfaces.
Dynamic loading initiates enhanced dislocation activity in the Co-free alloy.
Co normally modifies dislocation-core structure and stacking-fault energy in this alloy family.
The absence of Co changes local dislocation interactions and causes strain-induced restructuring at grain boundaries.
Dynamic amorphization or nano-refinement increases strain hardening during high-rate loading.
The deformation-induced interfacial substructure enhances or preserves ductility while increasing strength.
At low strain rates, Co-free FeNiCrMn may have slightly lower yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At low strain rates, Co-free FeNiCrMn should exhibit a conventional ductility response.
At high strain rates, Co-free FeNiCrMn should maintain or improve both ductility and strength relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The high-rate mechanical response of Co-free FeNiCrMn is temperature dependent.
Under comparable high-rate loading, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi forms less dynamically amorphized or ultra-nanocrystalline substructure than the Co-free alloy.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi follows a more conventional, dislocation-slip-dominated deformation response than the Co-free alloy.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to a non-precipitated, single-phase state below phase-transformation and recrystallization temperatures.
The critical strain-rate and temperature thresholds for formation of the proposed substructure are unknown.
